invariants: The home route renders its own bespoke in-hero A&J navigation instead of the shared Header, with links to /film, /gallery, /guestbook, /upload and /print plus the theme toggle.
The hero uses the poster image /images/home/intro-video-poster.png only — no local <video> element, no broken media source.
"Enter archive" scrolls to #welcome-panel; hero nav links route into the public experience.

dataSources: content:story.json (archival only: its consumers EngagementSection/StoryTimeline are unmounted)
content:timeline.json (archival only: its consumer StoryTimeline is unmounted)
invariants: 9 hard-coded milestone cards render in order Summer 2017 -> May 10 2025, including the Halloween-styled proposal card with its 8-photo carousel, per-card Read more/less expansion at 120 characters, the scroll-progress rail with heart marker and the closing film CTA card with the saved-progress resume label.
The live story copy lives in LoveTimeline.tsx; src/data/engagement.ts + src/data/timeline.ts are NOT rendered by any mounted component, so the rebuild must not present them as live content.
Home renders the shared Footer (but not the shared Header).

The countdown derives from the single WEDDING_DATE (2025-05-10T17:00:00-05:00): elapsed years/days after the date, a day/hour/minute/second countdown inside the 30-day pre-anniversary window, and the ordinal anniversary label.
Time-dependent copy is compared only under ui.json.fixedNow so text parity is stable across captures and machines.
The four editorial slot keys stay stable: home_moment_of_the_week, home_newest_standout_upload, home_featured_guestbook_note, film_featured_guest_video.
Inactive/absent slots render nothing (not an error); a DB error renders an accessible role=status banner naming the slot.
The guest highlight reel shows the top-6 photos by likes plus the 10 newest guestbook notes, rotates quotes with dot navigation and self-hides when both sources are empty.
The main film plays from /video/main.mp4 with poster /images/film/main-film-poster.png, preload=metadata, captions <track> /video/main.vtt with an aria-pressed toggle, and runtime label 45:53.

Player controls keep chapter menu + progress-bar chapter markers, 10 s skip, volume, fullscreen and cast when available; progress is saved under video-progress-main-film and the resume CTA (?resume=1) reads it.
Captions load from the configured media host and fail gracefully (non-WEBVTT response rejects) without breaking playback.
All ten chapter labels and timestamps remain: Start, Bachelor+ette, "Who Is It", Wedding Party, Our Vows, The Ceremony, The Reception, First Dance, Bloopers, The Party.

Chapter moment slugs (start, bachelor-ette, who-is-it, wedding-party, our-vows, the-ceremony, the-reception, first-dance, bloopers, the-party) stay stable because they are deep-link targets (?moment=<slug>).
When the chapters VTT is missing or returns HTML, the frozen fallback chapters are used — never an empty chapter list.
All four parent-dance films survive with ids, labels, descriptions, durations, thumbnails, video sources, VTT captions and four preview-frame timestamps: mom, melony, christine, jerame.
A family film deep link (?clip=<id>) opens the matching modal player and clears the param on close.
Thumbnails and captions resolve through the configured media host.
Only approved guest uploads with video_urls appear in the film highlights; archive_only rows are excluded unless featured; at most 6 clips render.
Each clip keeps its badge and memory-trail label (memoryTrails.ts), and memory-trail links (/film?moment=..., /film?clip=..., /gallery?collection=...) keep resolving.
The film_featured_guest_video editorial slot can promote one guest video above the rest.
The family-and-friends tree keeps both sides (bride's family, groom's family, bridesmaids, groomsmen) and shows first names up front.
Every card opens the member modal with full name, role, portrait and description/fun fact where present; mirror-image flags are preserved.
All 20 party members from partyData remain reachable with their portraits.

Exactly four collection tabs with this ?collection= vocabulary: Proposal | Bach+ette | Wedding Photos | Guest Photos (src/components/gallery/constants.ts:26); DB album aliases (Engagement, Wedding Day, Guest Uploads) are mapped to tabs and are NOT URL values.
The 35 curated photos always render even when Supabase fails; API rows are merged with de-duplication by id/url/thumbnail and likes/comments hydrated from RPCs.

Three view modes (masonry | grid | timeline) with aria-pressed state, per-tab counts and cover images, and infinite scroll ordered by album_sort_order then created_at (page sizes 12/18, scroll container resets on filter/view change).
Search covers caption, location, photographer, collection, source, face names and tags, and ?q=<query> pre-fills it.
All 9 gallery controls remain usable at 320 px and 390 px in both themes; view-mode buttons and collection chips expose aria-pressed state.
Filters compose (collection + query + view) and reset predictably; the empty-result state is deliberate.
The lightbox is a portal dialog (role=dialog, aria-modal) with focus trap + restore; Esc closes and left/right arrows navigate; ?photo=<id> and ?shared=<id> open the matching photo.

Photo details keep pinch/double-tap zoom 1-3x, face hotspots with verified-name badge, EXIF panel, likes, comments (author persisted in wedding-gallery-comment-author), download, share (?shared=) and the print modal with vendor cards.
Like counts and per-visitor like state come from the RPCs and update optimistically without losing the server count.
Comment author, content and relative timestamp formatting are preserved; comment counts stay in sync and comment writes stay behind the RPCs/RLS.
Per-browser engagement identity stays stable (getPhotoEngagementSessionId).
Selection is capped at 50 (with a toast); <=20 photos zip client-side, 21-50 POST to /.netlify/functions/download-pack; the queue persists in sessionStorage and shows progress states.
Original-file downloads return the original bytes (download_url || url), not thumbnails.
?share=<comma-separated ids> preselects and queues those photos and drives the gallery SEO/edge-OG image; the copy-link button shares that URL.
The claims wizard keeps its 4 steps: identity -> 6-digit code -> photo selection -> submitted; it is reachable from the /upload "Claim My Photos" CTA and submits photo_claims rows that start pending.
Claim verification in the frozen app is CLIENT-SIDE ONLY (A4 §6 finding S1); the rebuild must not present it as server-verified without an explicit owner decision.
Claim status transitions (pending -> approved/rejected, rejection reason) match the admin claims moderation queue, and guest identity emails are never rendered publicly.
Drag and keyboard reorder both work; photos can move between the 4 albums, bulk-move after an anchor / to top / to bottom, and delete with undo.
Only dirty diffs are saved through save_album_organization_v2; photo ids and URLs never change.
Search disables dragging so filtered views cannot silently reorder the archive.
Drag/drop or picker accepts images/video only with a 500 MB per-file cap; duplicate fingerprints are skipped and a stored queue shows a resume notice; images are compressed client-side.

Upload uses the pre-signed guest-upload-url function + R2 PUT with XHR progress and per-file retry; failure copy stays distinct for slot-unavailable / R2 PUT / timeout / size errors and hasErrors surfaces "Needs retry".

Submit is blocked until name+email are valid, inserts are retried 3x, and the success panel shows the share-token link; every row lands as status pending (moderation queue) and never publishes itself.
Messages render newest-first with nested comments and reaction counts; search covers name+content and "Read more notes" paginates by 8.
?message=<id> scrolls to + highlights the message and expands pages; a deep-linked message hidden by search clears the search instead of hiding.
Empty and error states are deliberate and accessible.
Validation stays name 2-50 chars / message 10-500 chars; the honeypot field silently succeeds for bots.
Client limiter is 3/min and the server RPC enforces 3 per minute with a graceful fallback insert; the optimistic prepend is reconciled and the form resets after 2.2 s.
Submissions are sanitized and never publish without moderation; no write bypasses the RPC/RLS.
All four reaction types survive: love, clap, laugh, wow; a per-browser fingerprint in localStorage prevents double-reacting.
Reactions increment/decrement optimistically with rollback on a failed PATCH; replies prepend optimistically and insert into guestbook_comments, keeping optimistic state on failure.
Reaction labels/icons stay stable so the reply/reaction UI does not silently change meaning.
Only approved guest uploads appear; pending/rejected rows are never listed publicly and guest emails are never rendered.
The page keeps upload counts, 6 featured thumbnails, and per-guest cards with name/date/photo count/message plus explicit empty and error states.
Every activity type renders its card with display name, preview and source link; filters keep All/Photos/Guestbook plus the moment type map.
Realtime INSERTs prepend via the new-activity banner; infinite scroll loads at the bottom and the empty state is deliberate.
Realtime subscription is disabled when window.__E2E__ is set so captures/tests are deterministic. Metadata is inherited/stale on this route (known defect, captured in rendered snapshots).
The token resolves a guest email and then that guest's uploads, guestbook notes and approved claimed photos; photos are de-duplicated across sources and stats counts are shown with a tab switch.
Title is dynamic (`<guest name>'s Album`), noindex, with a copy-link button (execCommand fallback) and lightbox like/comment; the page links back to /gallery.
An invalid/expired token shows the deliberate fallback state — never another guest's data and never an unhandled error.
Album toggles load on demand; the max-photos-per-album slider (6-200) plus numeric input (1-500) and the guestbook include toggle keep their behaviour; print is disabled when nothing is selected.
Print CSS hides header/footer/control panel, forces a white page background, sets letter-portrait @page margins and starts each album on a new page; browser Save-as-PDF remains the export path.
The route stays noindex with canonical /print and renders without the public Header/Footer/OfflineIndicator.
isAdmin is derived from app_metadata.role === 'admin' (never user metadata); the client check is UI-only and RLS stays authoritative.

Unauthenticated /admin and /admin/* redirect to /admin/login preserving the intended destination; authenticated visits to /admin/login redirect to /admin; a signed-in non-admin sees upgrade instructions instead of admin data.
Session persists in the Supabase localStorage key shape sb-<projectRef>-auth-token, refreshes, and is cleared by sign-out; admin pages are private and never indexable.
Dashboard counts (photos, pending uploads, guestbook messages, approved uploads) come from head+count probes and never load full rows.

The 10 admin child routes stay reachable from the dashboard/sidebar: /admin, /admin/photos, /admin/albums, /admin/review, /admin/claims, /admin/guestbook, /admin/featured, /admin/audit, /admin/analytics, /admin/settings.
Admin chrome keeps the desktop sidebar + mobile nav and exposes the signed-in admin email.
Admins can approve/reject/move-to-pending guest uploads, delete guestbook messages, and approve/reject claims with a required rejection reason; destructive actions are confirmed.
Every state change writes an audit entry with actor (userId, email, name), from/to status and summary; bulk actions log per item.
Moderation queues show guest names without leaking credentials; RLS still enforces access server-side.
All four slots are editable via the per-slot form (active, title, summary, badge, CTA, URL, source type); the active slot loads its row by slot key.
Saving upserts the slot and appends a history entry; deactivating a slot hides it on the public home/film surfaces.
Slot keys never change because they are the public→admin contract.
The audit log shows actor, action, entity, summary and timestamp for every moderation mutation (append-only from the UI).
Analytics aggregates stay read-only and label their sources; the Settings screen stays explicitly read-only operations notes (it must not pretend to persist settings the site does not store).
No secret, token or full email is rendered in these admin views beyond the signed-in admin's own email.

Per-route title/description/robots/canonical/OG/Twitter/JSON-LD match contracts/seo-pwa.json; the title pattern `<page> | Austin & Jordyn's Wedding` is preserved and noindex applies on /print, /admin/login, /guest/:token and the 404.
Structured data survives: WebSite+Event on home, VideoObject on film, ImageGallery on gallery, exactly one script tagged data-seo-structured-data.

The Netlify edge OG for /gallery?share=<id> still rewrites og:title/description/image and twitter equivalents from the photo row, falling through untouched on every failure. KNOWN DEFECT: /activity and all /admin/* pages set no metadata (inherited/stale); the rebuild must add per-route metadata rather than preserve the defect.

Manifest keeps name/short_name/display/start_url/theme/background/lang from seo-pwa.json plus 8 icons (maskable any) and 2 shortcuts (Gallery, Guest Book); the app registers an autoUpdate service worker with skipWaiting + clientsClaim and settles within <=2 document loads (no reload loop).

Service worker caching contract: CacheFirst for /media/_thumbs/* (max 500) and other /media/* (max 300), cacheable only status 200 (opaque status 0 excluded), 30-day expiry; legacy v1 caches purged on boot.
offline.html stays precached and the install prompt remains available; the app shell is usable offline for previously visited routes.

Security headers stay: X-Frame-Options DENY, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin, Permissions-Policy, HSTS, and the exact CSP allowlists (Supabase, Netlify, media host, R2, GA, Sentry ingest).
Cache headers stay: immutable /assets/*, no-store for /sw.js, /registerSW.js, /manifest.webmanifest, /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml.
Deployment routing stays: wedding.theporadas.com -> www 301 redirect and the SPA catch-all fallback to /index.html (200).
Any unmatched path (including the retired /people URL) renders the shared-shell 404 with noindex, nofollow and canonical /404; it never redirects or resurrects a page.
The 404 page keeps Header/Footer except on admin and print routes; the sitemap never lists a path that resolves to the catch-all.
The /people ghost is an explicit decision: legacy scripts/generate-sitemap.js emitted it, but the face-recognition People page was retired and /people must stay a noindex 404.
Every media path in contracts/content/MEDIA_MANIFEST.json resolves and original downloads still return original bytes; thumbnails/renditions/captions/posters are all represented.

Only /video/, /background_audio/ and /media/ are offloaded through VITE_MEDIA_BASE_URL (NOT /images/); path segments such as 'Bach+ette' and spaces in track filenames are preserved. The media worker keeps its CORS allowlist, Range/If-None-Match support, immutable cache headers and legacy->curated filename map.

No media bytes are copied into the greenfield repo; contracts reference paths only. Archival note: mainPlaylist/halloweenTrack are extracted for the archive, but BackgroundMusic has no importer — no music is mounted in the frozen app, so the rebuild needs an explicit owner decision before mounting it.
GA4 gtag loads only when VITE_GA_ID is present, with anonymize_ip, and a manual page_view per route carries path+title; with no ID nothing is injected.
Sentry initializes only when VITE_SENTRY_DSN is present, uses the deploy commit as release, strips PII in beforeSend, and source maps are uploaded then deleted from the published output.
CSP connect-src keeps the Sentry ingest host and GA endpoints allowlisted; analytics/error tracking never blocks render or leaks guest PII.
The skip link is the first Tab stop and focuses #main-content; there is exactly one main landmark with an aria-label that follows the route; route changes are announced politely.
Keyboard shortcuts survive: ? opens the shortcuts modal, Ctrl+K focuses search, Ctrl+T toggles theme, gallery arrows/Esc/L; modals trap focus and restore it to the trigger.
No critical axe violations on public or admin routes; reduced motion is honored where the frozen app honors it (not globally — e2e forces reducedMotion for every capture).

Both dark and light themes exist; the ui store persists currentTheme and ThemeController drives html[data-theme] + CSS variables. dark is the user-preference default (ui.json defaultTheme) — a starting preference, not a hard invariant.
The toggle and Ctrl+T switch themes; theme choice survives reload and does not change visible copy.
Parity/text comparisons run in both themes per contracts/ui.json, and the 9 gallery controls stay usable at 320/390 px in both.
